doc: Binary layout of the side store: one memory-mapped file shared by the live worker (spikes/ai-surround/live-worker.py, the only writer of everything but the player block) and the player (spikes/performer-p1, perf1 --ai-sides PATH, the only writer of the player block). Little-endian, every field naturally aligned. Python builds its numpy dtypes from this file (live/side_store.py); the C reader (src/perf1-ai-sides-store.h) mirrors it with static asserts, and the store self-test proves both agree. A change of any offset, size or meaning is a new schema_major (2: projective frame transforms and patch pages, phase 4). Regions, in file order: header (layout, worker and player blocks), frame table, shot table, canvas records (one per heap slot), heap (slots of heap_slot_bytes each, holding a canvas's pixels or a shot's patch page). TIMELINE and SPACE follow the content model (spikes/film-analysis/schema/common.schema.json): film time is seconds on the rebased timeline (first frame = 0, the player's frame time bit for bit), positions are pixels of the stored video frame, continuous (pixel u spans [u, u + 1), its centre at u + 0.5). WORLD: each canvas id (a set of shots that show one place) has its own world coordinates; a frame's transform maps its source pixels to them. CONSISTENCY: records that change after they are first published carry a sequence counter (frame.seq, shot.seq, canvas.gen, player.seq): the writer makes it odd, writes the fields, then makes it even; a reader copies the record and keeps the copy only if the counter was even and unchanged across the copy. A frame's pts, the layout block and the file size never change while store_uid stays the same.

layout.doc: Written once by the worker that creates the file, before worker.state becomes running.

fields.name: magic
fields.doc: b'PNRSIDE2'

fields.name: schema_minor
fields.doc: 0; a reader of the same major accepts any minor

fields.name: file_bytes
fields.doc: size of the whole store file

fields.name: max_frames
fields.doc: rows of the frame table

fields.name: max_shots
fields.doc: rows of the shot table

fields.name: heap_slots
fields.doc: canvas records, one per heap slot

fields.name: heap_slot_bytes
fields.doc: bytes of one heap slot (a multiple of 4096)

fields.name: off_frames
fields.doc: file offset of the frame table

fields.name: off_shots
fields.doc: file offset of the shot table

fields.name: off_canvases
fields.doc: file offset of the canvas records

fields.name: off_heap
fields.doc: file offset of heap slot 0 (a multiple of 4096)

fields.name: store_uid
fields.doc: random id of this file's contents; a new one whenever the worker re-creates the store, so the player drops everything it cached from the old one

worker.doc: Written by the worker only; each field is read on its own (aligned 4- and 8-byte values are read whole).

fields.name: state
fields.doc: worker_state enum

fields.name: beat
fields.doc: grows about 10 times a second while the worker lives; the player calls the worker lost when it stops for 2 s

fields.name: qpc
fields.doc: QueryPerformanceCounter at the last beat

fields.name: film_bytes
fields.doc: size of the film file the store describes (the player checks it against its own file)

fields.name: src_w
fields.doc: stored picture size of the film

fields.name: frames_published
fields.doc: frame-table rows whose pts are set: [0, frames_published) (raised only after their pts are written)

fields.name: shots_published
fields.doc: shot-table rows in use: [0, shots_published)

fields.name: analysed_frames
fields.doc: frames with a valid transform (diagnostic)

fields.name: painter_state
fields.doc: painter_state enum

fields.name: plates_skipped
fields.doc: plates not made because their shot was too short or could not be ready before it started

fields.name: cache_hits
fields.doc: canvases served from the disk cache

fields.name: throttle_events
fields.doc: times the worker held GPU work back because the player reported late frames or low slack

fields.name: painter_s_per_plate
fields.doc: running estimate the scheduler uses

fields.name: epoch_seen
fields.doc: the player epoch (seek counter) the worker has re-planned for

fields.name: film_name
fields.doc: UTF-8 base name of the film, NUL-padded

fields.name: status
fields.doc: short ASCII status for logs

player.doc: Written by the player only, under seq. The worker follows the playhead and the GPU pressure from it.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: sequence counter of this block

fields.name: beat
fields.doc: grows with every write (each master refresh)

fields.name: qpc
fields.doc: QueryPerformanceCounter at the last write

fields.name: state
fields.doc: player_state enum

fields.name: epoch
fields.doc: seek counter: changes at every seek and at the film start

fields.name: playhead_s
fields.doc: film time the master monitor shows now

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: film seconds per wall second (0 while paused)

fields.name: slack_ms
fields.doc: smallest present lead (planned refresh time minus the present call) over the last 0.5 s, all monitors

fields.name: late_recent
fields.doc: refreshes without a new present in the last 1 s, all monitors

fields.name: need_margin_px
fields.doc: how far leftover pixels reach beyond the crop, source px, left/top/right/bottom: the largest over the cue sheet's shots and all monitors (the side area the worker must cover)

fields.name: need_valid
fields.doc: 1 when need_margin_px is set

fields.name: src_w
fields.doc: the player's picture size (the worker checks it against its own)

fields.name: uploading_slot
fields.doc: heap slot the player is copying to the GPU now (-1: none); the worker must not reuse it

fields.name: uploading_gen
fields.doc: that slot's gen when the copy started

fields.name: showing_shot
fields.doc: shot on screen (-1: none known)

fields.name: showing_tier
fields.doc: tier on screen (0 glow)

fields.name: showing_canvas
fields.doc: canvas id on screen (-1: glow)

fields.name: resident_n
fields.doc: canvases on the GPU now

fields.name: resident_canvas
fields.doc: their canvas ids (diagnostic)

fields.name: uploads_torn
fields.doc: copies dropped because the slot changed under them

frame.doc: One row per frame of the film's frame table (the content model's rows, the player's frames). pts is written before frames_published covers the row and never changes. The rest is the side plan for that frame, written when its shot is analysed.

fields.name: pts
fields.doc: film time of the frame, seconds

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: sequence counter of the fields below

fields.name: shot
fields.doc: row in the shot table, -1 while not analysed

fields.name: h
fields.doc: the frame's camera transform, projective: source px (x, y) -> world px of its canvas: d = h6 x + h7 y + 1, wx = (h0 x + h1 y + h2) / d, wy = (h3 x + h4 y + h5) / d (a translation, or a homography where the camera model measured one: live/camera_model.py)

fields.name: gain
fields.doc: linear-light gain of the canvas colour on the left/top/right/bottom side (1 = none); for now one value for all four: the picture's mean linear luma over its median over the shot's lit kept frames (a fade's dark frames left out), through a soft knee (analyse_v0)

fields.name: state
fields.doc: step state per side, left/top/right/bottom (step_state enum; the step planner's, live/step_planner.py; the player ignores it)

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: frame_flags bits

shot.doc: One row per shot the worker knows. Rows are added in any order (after a seek the worker starts in the middle); a row describes a frame range, and frames name their row.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: sequence counter

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: shot_flags bits

fields.name: canvas_id
fields.doc: the set's canvas id (v1: the shot's own row)

fields.name: key_frame
fields.doc: frame whose source px the world px equal (v1: the shot's first frame)

fields.name: crop
fields.doc: crop the analysis took as the picture, source px [x0, y0, x1, y1)

fields.name: start_s
fields.doc: cue-sheet start: halfway between the shot's first frame and the frame before it (0 for the first shot)

fields.name: end_s
fields.doc: the next shot's start

fields.name: best_tier
fields.doc: best tier made for its canvas so far (diagnostic)

canvas.doc: One record per heap slot: what the slot holds, a canvas version (kind canvas) or a shot's patch page (kind patch_page). A canvas version is an RGBA image of a set's world: texel (i, j) covers world px [x0 + i * scale, x0 + (i + 1) * scale) x [y0 + j * scale, ...). A patch page is the slot laid out as the patch_page record, its patch table, then (from page_header_bytes) the packed RGBA8 texels of tex_w x tex_h at row_bytes; world_x0, world_y0 and scale are unused (the page's grid map says where its patches go). The worker writes the slot while gen is odd and state is free, then sets state complete and makes gen even; to reuse a slot it makes gen odd first. The player shows a canvas version, and a shot's patch page, only from the first frame of a showing (a cut, a seek, the film start) and only if they were on the GPU by then.

fields.name: gen
fields.doc: sequence counter of the slot (record and pixels)

fields.name: state
fields.doc: canvas_state enum

fields.name: version
fields.doc: grows with every new version of a canvas id; (canvas_id, version, recipe) names the pixels

fields.name: tier
fields.doc: tier enum

fields.name: format
fields.doc: pixel_format enum

fields.name: shot_hint
fields.doc: the shot it was made for (diagnostic)

fields.name: world_x0
fields.doc: world px at the left edge of texel column 0

fields.name: world_y0
fields.doc: world px at the top edge of texel row 0

fields.name: scale
fields.doc: world px per texel

fields.name: valid_from_s
fields.doc: start of the showing it was made for; the player never shows it for frames before that

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: pixel bytes in the slot: tex_h * row_bytes

fields.name: recipe
fields.doc: hash of how it was made (analysis and painter versions, scale, margins)

fields.name: made_qpc
fields.doc: QueryPerformanceCounter when it was completed

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: canvas_kind enum

fields.name: shot
fields.doc: patch page: the shot row its patches belong to (-1 for a canvas)

fields.name: page_header_bytes
fields.doc: patch page: bytes before its texels (the patch_page record and its patch table, rounded up to 4096)

fields.name: n_patches
fields.doc: patch page: rows of its patch table

patch_page.doc: Start of a heap slot that holds a shot's patch page (structure path, live/structure.py). The page grid is the player's accumulate and overlay textures: grid_w x grid_h texels; grid_map takes the set's world px to a grid texel coordinate (texel i spans [i, i + 1)). The patch table (n_patches patch records) follows at byte 256.

fields.name: magic
fields.doc: b'PNRPAGE1'

fields.name: shot
fields.doc: the shot row

fields.name: first_frame
fields.doc: the shot's first frame (a check)

fields.name: n_frames
fields.doc: the shot's frames (a check)

fields.name: grid_map
fields.doc: 3x3, row-major: set world px (x, y, 1) -> page grid texel coordinate (homogeneous)

patch.doc: One patch of a page, in film-frame order. persistent: from film frame `frame` on, its texels replace the accumulate texture's at the destination rect (straight alpha: alpha 0 texels keep what is there); the player applies every persistent patch up to the frame on screen, in table order. overlay: shown over the rest for frames frame..until. The player composites overlay over accumulate over the base canvas, all sampled through the frame's transform.

fields.name: frame
fields.doc: film frame (frame-table row) from which it applies

fields.name: until
fields.doc: overlay: last frame (inclusive); persistent: 0xFFFFFFFF

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: patch_kind enum

fields.name: side
fields.doc: 0 left, 1 top, 2 right, 3 bottom, 255 unknown (diagnostic)

fields.name: dst_x
fields.doc: destination rect in the page grid, texels

fields.name: src_x
fields.doc: source rect's corner in the page's packed texels

formats.rgba8_film: 4 bytes per texel, rows of row_bytes: R, G, B as the film's own encoded values (BT.709 matrix, full range, the transfer the player decodes as BT.1886 with a true-black display, i.e. linear = code^2.4), A = coverage (straight alpha, 255 = fully covered). Uncovered texels carry their nearest covered colour so filtering never pulls in black.
formats.rgba16f_linear: reserved for a later minor version: half floats, linear light BT.709, premultiplied
